title: The Ruined Nobleman and the Loyal Singer
summary: Ali bin Mansur was an affluent young nobleman of Baghdad who squandered his vast inheritance through reckless generosity to false friends until he was left without a single dirh...
keywords: the ruined man of baghdad and his slave-girl
full_text:
Ali bin Mansur was an affluent young nobleman of Baghdad who squandered his vast inheritance through reckless generosity to false friends until he was left without a single dirham. He possessed only his modest house and a gifted maiden named Tawaddud, whom he had educated from childhood in poetry, calligraphy, and the lute.

Facing starvation, Tawaddud said with tears of noble loyalty: 'Take me to the slave market, master, and sell me to the Caliph’s court; my training will bring thousands of dinars to relieve your distress.'

With a breaking heart, Ali brought her to the market, where the royal purchaser of Caliph Harun al-Rashid bought her for ten thousand gold dinars.

When Ali took the gold and turned homeward, the emptiness of his house struck him with unbearable grief; he realized that all the gold of the empire could not replace the faithful soul who had shared his life.

At that same hour in the imperial palace, Tawaddud stood before Harun al-Rashid. Asked to perform, she touched her lute and sang a song of heartbreaking sorrow, describing her master’s nobility, his poverty, and how their hearts were torn asunder by cruel necessity.

Harun al-Rashid was moved to tears by her profound fidelity. The Caliph summoned Ali bin Mansur, returned Tawaddud to his arms, granted them the ten thousand gold dinars as a wedding gift, and appointed Ali to a high office in the royal granaries, praising the loyalty that chooses honor over gold.
moral: Selfless fidelity and artistic excellence in adversity restore fortune and inspire royal generosity.
